clue.text: Member in current international band of armed fighters

indicators.note: in tells us the Member's letters sit between the letters for current and international

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician belongs to a cross-border group of militants.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors under arms.

clue.text: London museum bearing down on large destructive thug

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, pressing down on, the second

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big brute is being pursued by a London museum, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A (Victoria and Albert Museum) is spelt out as V AND A, so its letters are VANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wrecks property out of sheer malice, a destructive hooligan.

clue.text: Cross individual picked up short call for old historian

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to phone is to call

explanation.surface: An angry lone person picks up a curtailed phone call about an ancient chronicler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns ONE into ENO; 'short' docks PHONE to PHON.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophon was an ancient Athenian soldier who wrote histories such as the Anabasis.

clue.text: After removal of cap, made case for this sort of petrol?

indicators.note: the cap of a down word is its top letter, which is removed here

parts.note: to make a case is to plead, so made case means pleaded

explanation.surface: Someone argued for fuel of an old kind once the price cap went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After removal of cap' takes P from the top of PLEADED. The question mark covers the definition by reference: petrol is the kind with the additive.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaded petrol contained tetraethyl lead as an anti-knock additive, now largely banned.

clue.text: Performer against restraining press

indicators.note: restraining means holding inside, so the outer word clasps the inner

parts.note: con is a word for against, as in pros and cons
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: An entertainer is opposed to gagging the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' reads as censorship of the press, but it only signals one piece holding another.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a stand-up or comic actor, a kind of entertainer on stage.

clue.text: Hollow place for storing complete dinosaur

parts.note: a dip is a hollow in the ground

indicators.note: storing means holding something within, so the place word holds the next

parts.note: a locus is a place or position
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: A sunken spot is wanted to keep an entire prehistoric reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complete' is a verb here, as in doing a job, not an adjective describing the dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplodocus is a long-necked sauropod from the Jurassic, one of the best-known prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: Mike weakens absurd workloads

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: absurd says the letters of the following word are thrown into a silly order

explanation.surface: A man called Mike is feeble about ridiculous amounts of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' rearranges WEAKENS into ANWEEKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-weeks measure labour as one person's work over a week, a way of sizing a job's effort.

clue.text: Reach to embrace excellent American friend

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping around, so the reach word encloses the next

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
rad is American slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone stretches to hug a great American pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excellent American' points to US slang rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or fellow member, a close mate.

clue.text: Mentioned more than just a neat seaside town

indicators.note: mentioned means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a neat is an old word for one head of cattle, so more than one are cows

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a tidy coastal resort, and something more than tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy here but an archaic noun for a bovine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes is a sailing resort on the Isle of Wight, famous for its regatta week.

clue.text: Books in Morecambe, maybe adult smut?

indicators.note: in places the books inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, so Eric is one example of a Morecambe
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A collection of books in a Lancashire seaside town may be grown-up filth.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the seaside town but is Eric Morecambe, the British comic of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually explicit writing or art, which a prude would call filth.

clue.text: Tense, taking ecstasy too early — that's odd

indicators.note: ecstasy is E, and taking it too early moves that letter forward in the word

parts.note: wired means tense and jumpy

explanation.surface: Someone on edge popped a pill before time, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ecstasy too early' moves the E in WIRED one place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird means strange or uncanny, which is what something odd is.

clue.text: In opposition, even lady invites chap in fraternity

indicators.note: in opposition says each of the next words is swapped for its opposite

parts.note: the opposite of even is odd
the opposite of a lady is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A smooth-faced opposition woman asks a man to join a brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word of 'even lady' is replaced by its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, a mutual-aid brotherhood whose members bear that title.

clue.text: Crush rat running out of a church

indicators.note: running out of a means the word has its A used up and removed

parts.note: to rat on someone is to squeal, to inform

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a rodent that is fleeing a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a verb meaning to inform, SQUEAL; 'running out of a' drops its A to give SQUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To squelch is to crush or squash flat, especially to suppress something.

clue.text: Calm, having folded head to toe after bad turn

indicators.note: after puts the folded piece behind the mangled one
bad signals that the following word's letters are mangled
head to toe says the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: to double paper is to fold it

explanation.surface: Someone stays serene, having bent over head to feet after a nasty spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges TURN to UNTR; 'head to toe' sends the D of DOUBLE to its end, giving OUBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Untroubled means free of worry or disturbance, serene and composed.

clue.text: Decline to turn left into empty drive

indicators.note: into puts the twisting piece and the left letter inside the emptied drive
empty removes the inner letters, leaving only the outside ones

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to swing left onto a vacant driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a refusal but is the definition, meaning to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to decline, shrinking gradually in size or number.

clue.text: Can't industrious criminal play?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrongly done, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A query whether a hard-working crook can't be dramatised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges CANT INDUSTRIOUS; the apostrophe is ignored. The play is fittingly full of crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is Shakespeare's early revenge tragedy, notorious for its bloodshed.

clue.text: Acidic, ferocious sort starts to intimidate colleagues

parts.note: a tartar is a fierce, violent person

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A sour, savage type begins bullying co-workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartaric acid is found in grapes, so tartaric describes something of that acid's kind.

clue.text: Notorious influencer against returning non-British resident of Bangladesh

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read back to front

parts.note: VS is versus, against

indicators.note: non-British says the letter B for British is removed

parts.note: a Bengali is someone from Bengal, which includes Bangladesh

explanation.surface: A notorious social-media figure opposes the return of a foreign Bangladeshi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns VS into SV; 'non-British' takes B from BENGALI to leave ENGALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, names anyone with sinister control over another.

clue.text: My word — running around is antisocial behaviour

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters go round the little word
running suggests the letters flow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock: racing about is hooliganism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My word' is an exclamation in the surface but supplies plain letters; 'running' is the anagram signal and 'around' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is rough, noisy, disorderly conduct, the behaviour of hooligans.

clue.text: Their employment levels typically exceed those of their clients

definitions.text: Their employment levels typically exceed those of their clients

parts.words: Their employment levels typically exceed those of their clients
parts.note: it reads as a job statistic, but these tradesmen literally work higher up than the people below them

explanation.surface: A statement about an occupation with more work than its customers have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'levels' means height, not rates: these tradespeople work on top of the house while the householder stays below.
explanation.definitionFit: These tradespeople fix tiles and slates on top of buildings, physically above their customers.

clue.text: Person finally squeezed into retro jeans, showing blubber

indicators.note: squeezed into says a letter is forced inside the next piece
retro means backward-looking, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Levis are a brand of jeans

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone at last forces their way into vintage denim and is seen weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns LEVIS into SIVEL; 'finally' gives N from Person, which goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob noisily, to whimper and weep.

clue.text: Doodah's wife claims to keep time

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the claim phrase holds the time letter

parts.note: has it, as in 'rumour has it', means claims

explanation.surface: A man's spouse insists on keeping time for him.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS IT ('claims', as in 'rumour has it') holds T to make HATSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah, like a thingummy, is a word for an object whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Author translated bible including an abridged Apostle

indicators.note: including says the bible letters hold the shortened apostle

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version, the King James translation of the Bible

indicators.note: abridged says the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Simon Peter is an apostle

explanation.surface: A writer rendered scripture, putting in a cut-down account of an apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated bible' is the Authorized Version, the standard English translation; 'abridged' drops the apostle's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction writer, author of I, Robot.

clue.text: Perhaps Mary Magdalene returned, evil finally purged in Pentateuch

indicators.note: purged means a letter is cleared out of the word
returned means read back to front

parts.note: Mary Magdalene was traditionally, if wrongly, described as a prostitute

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Maybe a biblical figure came back, with the last of evil cleansed, in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives TOLRAH; 'purged' removes the L that 'finally' takes from evil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, the Mosaic law.

clue.text: Double meaning by a doctor, one responsible for cutting line

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cutting means a letter is cut away from the word

parts.note: guilty means responsible for a wrong

explanation.surface: A doctor creates a pun, someone being to blame for cutting a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting line' removes L from GUILTY to give GUITY. 'one responsible' looks like a unit, but they are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiguity is the quality of being open to more than one interpretation.

clue.text: Suffer strain, curable only partly

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A disease strain can only partly be cured, to the patient's suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it, bringing it on oneself.

clue.text: Persuade scholar, off and on, to provide leader for Times

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of the second, leading it
off and on means every other letter is taken, skipping the rest

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Someone talks an academic into writing a lead article for The Times now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of scholar, COA; 'leader' is not an editorial but a piece in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to wheedle or cajole someone gently into doing something.

clue.text: Marine object that is intercepted by top executive guarding Florida

indicators.note: intercepted by means the abbreviation is broken into by what follows

parts.note: IE stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding something protectively

parts.note: CEO is the chief executive officer
FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A naval craft is stopped by a company boss who protects the Sunshine State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' nests Florida inside the boss, and 'intercepted by' sets that whole unit inside the abbreviation for that is.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice floe is a sheet of floating ice, a thing found at sea.

clue.text: Bear with appetite

definitions.meaning: to bear something is to tolerate or put up with it
an appetite is a desire or liking, as in having no taste for a fight

explanation.surface: An animal with a big hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach is to endure, and having the stomach for something means having the appetite for it.
